sourceReferences.title: Anacropora Ridley, 1884 genus record (accepted; family Acroporidae). Description after Veron (1986): colonies arborescent with thin tapered branches, without axial corallites; all corallites radial, small and immersed; septa in two cycles; columellae absent; corallite walls and coenosteum porous without elaborations; polyps extended day and night, widely spaced, small, with fine tentacles. Type species Anacropora forbesi Ridley, 1884.
sourceReferences.publisher: World Register of Marine Species (World List of Scleractinia, Hoeksema & Cairns)

sourceReferences.title: Anacropora forbesi species factsheet: branches evenly spaced, less than 10 mm thick and tapered with blunt tips; corallites with slightly prominent lower lips; coenosteum smooth; colour pale brown with white branch tips; shallow, usually turbid reef environments; the type species of the genus and a species complex.
sourceReferences.publisher: Corals of the World (Veron, Stafford-Smith, Turak, DeVantier; Australian Institute of Marine Science)
sourceReferences.license: Text facts cited only; no imagery used

sourceReferences.title: Anacropora puertogalerae species factsheet: branches compact, less than 13 mm thick and tapering to a point; corallites widely spaced; the lower lip of corallites commonly spine-like; colour pale brown, sometimes with white branch tips; a species complex.
sourceReferences.publisher: Corals of the World (Veron, Stafford-Smith, Turak, DeVantier; Australian Institute of Marine Science)
sourceReferences.license: Text facts cited only; no imagery used

sourceReferences.title: Reef Corals of the Indo-Malayan Seas, genus Anacropora (after Veron and Wallace 1984): zooxanthellate, thinly branched with no axial polyp, not encrusting at the base; polyps small (up to 1 mm in diameter), inconspicuous, slightly or not protruding; coenosteum smooth from fine, evenly distributed granulated spines; colour predominantly brown, branch tips may appear white from the local absence of zooxanthellae; sheltered, silt-tolerant habitats.
sourceReferences.license: Text facts cited only; no imagery used

sourceReferences.title: Pillai, C. S. G. (1973). A review of the genus Anacropora Ridley (Scleractinia, Acroporidae) with the description of a new species. Branches of the type slender, 2.2 to 2.5 mm thick, branchlets equal in thickness to the main branches, apices obtuse; corallites projecting with walls 0.9 to 1.1 mm high, openings 0.8 to 0.9 mm, adjacent corallites 2.5 to 3 mm apart; septa in two cycles.
sourceReferences.publisher: Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI eprints)
sourceReferences.license: Institutional repository text; facts cited only

sourceReferences.title: Anacropora (briar corals): fragile corals with branches less than ten centimetres long forming small colonies, branches spreading or clustered and sometimes fused; calices rounded and up to one millimetre in diameter; coenosteum porous with small tubercles; no axial corallites; delicate tentacles often extended by day. Seven species listed.
